main.title: Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars
main.summary: Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars is a 2009 action-adventure game developed by Rockstar Leeds in conjunction with Rockstar North and published by Rockstar Games.

cards.heading: Huang Lee's route through Liberty City
cards.text: Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars is a 2009 action-adventure game developed by Rockstar Leeds in conjunction with Rockstar North and published by Rockstar Games. The game was released for the Nintendo DS in March 2009, PlayStation Portable in October 2009, iOS in January 2010, and Android and Fire OS devices in December 2014. It is the thirteenth game in the Grand Theft Auto series and a follow-up to Grand Theft Auto IV, and is the first entry to be released for handheld consoles since 2006's Vice City Stories. Set within modern-day Liberty City (a fictional satire of New York City), the single-player story follows young Triad member Huang Lee and his efforts to recover a sword gifted by his late father after it is stolen from him, while inadvertently becoming caught in a power struggle amongst Liberty City's Triads.

cards.heading: Touch controls and a trading economy
cards.text: The game was fundamentally designed for players to have notable interactions with objects on the DS and smartphone systems via their touch-screen controls, while offering unique elements of gameplay not found in other entries within the Grand Theft Auto series. The most notable element, the ability to buy drugs from suppliers and sell them to dealers to make money, proved controversial following the game's release. Despite this, the game received critical acclaim.

cards.heading: The Nintendo DS touch screen
cards.text: The Nintendo DS version of the game takes advantage of the touchscreen with functions such as controlling the PDA, GPS, the radio, access to the people on the map, or using Molotov cocktails and grenades. The top screen shows the game and storyboard. Taxi whistling is supported by the DS microphone or by holding the X button. Competitive and co-operative multiplayer modes are only available through DS to DS local wireless.

main.title: Guitar Hero: Metallica
main.subtitle: The whole band, at full force
main.summary: Metallica’s repertoire brings guitars, drums and vocals together, with a demanding new double-bass challenge.

cards.heading: A full-band tribute
cards.text: Guitar Hero: Metallica builds on World Tour’s four-player band format, supporting lead guitar, bass, drums and vocals. Metallica’s songs sit alongside pieces by other artists selected for the game, turning the setlist into both a portrait of the band and a broader hard-rock conversation. The group’s members contributed motion capture, and the venues draw on its imagery, album themes and live identity.

cards.heading: Keeping up with the drums
cards.text: The drum part received particular attention. Expert+ adds double-bass patterns for players using a second kick pedal, while practice tools help break difficult passages into manageable sections. Guitar, bass and vocal players still take part in the same shared performance rather than a separate drum-only game. Alongside career progression, the game retained competitive and music-creation features derived from World Tour, with Metallica-specific instrument sounds and presentation.

main.title: The Dishwasher: Dead Samurai
main.subtitle: A dishwasher fights through a hand-drawn nightmare
main.summary: The Dishwasher: Dead Samurai is James Silva's side-scrolling action game for Xbox Live Arcade, released on 1 April 2009. An unnamed dishwasher battles through waves of enemies using increasingly elaborate weapons and combinations. Its scratchy, hand-drawn appearance gives the violent action a restless visual identity. The player begins with meat cleavers before acquiring equipment that changes the possibilities within a fight. A level becomes a continuous effort to connect attacks, stay mobile and recognise when a weakened opponent can be finished before the next group closes in.

cards.heading: A dishwasher fights through a hand-drawn nightmare
cards.text: The Dishwasher: Dead Samurai is James Silva's side-scrolling action game for Xbox Live Arcade, released on 1 April 2009. An unnamed dishwasher battles through waves of enemies using increasingly elaborate weapons and combinations. Its scratchy, hand-drawn appearance gives the violent action a restless visual identity. The player begins with meat cleavers before acquiring equipment that changes the possibilities within a fight. A level becomes a continuous effort to connect attacks, stay mobile and recognise when a weakened opponent can be finished before the next group closes in.

cards.heading: Keep the combination moving
cards.text: Basic attacks, stronger strikes and grabs can be linked into combinations, while vulnerable enemies allow finishing moves that provide additional points and health. Defeated opponents leave spirals that support upgrades, and later weapons include a katana, firearms and a chainsaw. Dish Magic adds another resource to the available responses. The player has to make those tools work together against groups rather than treating each enemy as an isolated duel. A good sequence creates space, rewards the finishing blow and places the character where the next attack can begin without losing momentum.

cards.heading: A personal project reaches the console storefront
cards.text: Silva's idea grew from his own work as a dishwasher and eventually took shape using XNA Game Studio Express. Winning Microsoft's 2007 Dream-Build-Play competition brought a publishing contract for Xbox Live Arcade. Challenge and Arcade modes concentrate the combat into different arrangements, while cooperative play allows other players to join the action. A guitar minigame even supports familiar music-game peripherals. The game's arrival demonstrated how an individual creator could use accessible development tools and a digital console storefront to bring a strongly personal visual style and demanding action system to a broad audience.

main.title: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky
main.subtitle: Wake up as a Pokémon
main.summary: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky is Chunsoft's expanded Nintendo DS role-playing adventure built on Explorers of Time and Explorers of Darkness. A human transformed into a Pokémon joins a partner and becomes part of an exploration team. Their work takes them into shifting dungeons, where movement, supplies and turn-based encounters determine whether a mission can be completed safely. The premise places the creatures themselves at the centre of the story. Choosing a partner becomes the beginning of a relationship with somebody who shares both the danger and the discoveries.

cards.heading: Wake up as a Pokémon
cards.text: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky is Chunsoft's expanded Nintendo DS role-playing adventure built on Explorers of Time and Explorers of Darkness. A human transformed into a Pokémon joins a partner and becomes part of an exploration team. Their work takes them into shifting dungeons, where movement, supplies and turn-based encounters determine whether a mission can be completed safely. The premise places the creatures themselves at the centre of the story. Choosing a partner becomes the beginning of a relationship with somebody who shares both the danger and the discoveries.

cards.heading: A dungeon changes one turn at a time
cards.text: The party explores a grid of rooms and corridors whose arrangement can change between visits. Movement gives nearby enemies an opportunity to act, so stepping toward an item or another passage is also a tactical choice. Supplies and the condition of the team affect how far it is sensible to continue. This rhythm makes exploration and fighting part of the same activity. The next decision may be a simple movement across one square, but it can expose the partner to another attack or bring the pair closer to a needed resource.

cards.heading: More lives around the central journey
cards.text: Explorers of Sky adds playable starting choices and Special Episodes that develop supporting characters beyond their roles in the main adventure. Those additions explain its identity as an expanded edition rather than a separate beginning to the exploration story. The central partnership still provides its emotional anchor, while the additional perspectives make the surrounding cast more substantial. A game about finding one's place among Pokémon gains from allowing other members of that world to have journeys of their own, including circumstances the main pair would not otherwise experience.

main.title: Little King's Story
main.subtitle: A small crown brings a large responsibility
main.summary: Little King's Story is Cing and Town Factory's Wii adventure combining real-time strategy with the management of a growing kingdom. Corobo, a timid boy who discovers a mysterious crown, gains the ability to command people and becomes ruler of Alpoko. Leading citizens into the surrounding countryside provides treasure and opportunities to expand the settlement. Their different occupations turn the population into both a community and the means of exploring beyond it. The kingdom begins modestly, giving each new building and newly trained follower a visible place in its development.

cards.heading: A small crown brings a large responsibility
cards.text: Little King's Story is Cing and Town Factory's Wii adventure combining real-time strategy with the management of a growing kingdom. Corobo, a timid boy who discovers a mysterious crown, gains the ability to command people and becomes ruler of Alpoko. Leading citizens into the surrounding countryside provides treasure and opportunities to expand the settlement. Their different occupations turn the population into both a community and the means of exploring beyond it. The kingdom begins modestly, giving each new building and newly trained follower a visible place in its development.

cards.heading: Take the right citizens beyond the gate
cards.text: Corobo gathers followers and directs individuals toward work, obstacles or enemies. A farmer can dig effectively but is poorly suited to a fight, while a soldier's strengths do not solve every problem in the landscape. Training facilities change citizens' occupations, so preparing an expedition involves deciding what kinds of help the next route requires. The group remains physically present around its king, making an order an action performed by a particular person. Success depends on using the population's different abilities rather than treating every follower as an interchangeable unit.

cards.heading: A kingdom has days of its own
cards.text: Treasure and successful expeditions finance new buildings, while requests placed in the town's suggestion box provide additional work for Corobo. The settlement also marks major events with celebrations that can interrupt the usual routine of issuing commands. These details give the people a role beyond serving as a resource for the next campaign. Returning home allows the player to see the effects of expansion, adjust the workforce and hear another complaint. The adventure's larger ambitions grow from a place whose daily activity becomes increasingly familiar as its borders spread.

main.title: Punch-Out!!
main.subtitle: Little Mac returns to the ring
main.summary: Punch-Out!! is Next Level Games' Wii boxing game bringing Little Mac back through a series of highly individual opponents. Familiar fighters return alongside new faces, with exaggerated animation making each rival's personality and habits readable from the opposite side of the ring. The player blocks, dodges and counters rather than moving freely around an arena. Progress comes from recognising a particular opponent's routine and finding a safe opening. The reboot gives the established contest a more expressive presentation while keeping the careful reading of an incoming attack at its centre.

cards.heading: Little Mac returns to the ring
cards.text: Punch-Out!! is Next Level Games' Wii boxing game bringing Little Mac back through a series of highly individual opponents. Familiar fighters return alongside new faces, with exaggerated animation making each rival's personality and habits readable from the opposite side of the ring. The player blocks, dodges and counters rather than moving freely around an arena. Progress comes from recognising a particular opponent's routine and finding a safe opening. The reboot gives the established contest a more expressive presentation while keeping the careful reading of an incoming attack at its centre.

cards.heading: A grin can be an opening
cards.text: Certain moments in an opponent's animation allow Little Mac to earn a star by landing a well-timed punch. Stars power stronger attacks, but taking a hit loses the collected reward. Ordinary punches and defensive actions also affect the heart counter, which can leave Mac temporarily unable to attack when exhausted. These systems make patience useful. A missed opportunity may be safer than a careless exchange, while recognising the right gesture allows a small, precise response to become a much more damaging punch at the moment it is needed.

cards.heading: Winning the belt changes the opponents
cards.text: The initial climb through the circuits leads to Title Defense, where returning opponents use new techniques and protections. King Hippo, for example, arrives with a manhole cover protecting his stomach, changing the familiar problem of reaching his vulnerable spot. Players can use motion controls with the Remote and Nunchuk or hold the Remote sideways for traditional button inputs. The alternative arrangements serve the same encounters, allowing the timing and observation to remain central even when the player's preferred way of throwing a punch changes between control schemes.

main.title: inFAMOUS
main.subtitle: Electrical powers across Empire City
main.summary: Sucker Punch released inFAMOUS for PlayStation 3 in the United States on May 26, 2009.

cards.heading: Cole after the explosion
cards.text: Sucker Punch released inFAMOUS for PlayStation 3 in the United States on May 26, 2009. An explosion leaves Empire City devastated and gives Cole MacGrath electrical powers. He climbs its buildings, follows rails and cables, and fights from the streets and rooftops. His decisions also shape how citizens respond to him.

cards.heading: Routes above the streets
cards.text: Ledges, pipes, signs and other architectural features give Cole routes up and across buildings. Rooftops form an alternative to travelling at street level. Reaching higher ground also changes combat, offering new angles for attacks and protection from enemies below.

cards.heading: Moving through an electrical city
cards.text: Cole can draw energy from parts of the city and move quickly along cables and rails. The same electrical powers support ranged attacks and traversal. Infrastructure that appears ordinary at street level becomes a source of energy or a route once the player learns to use it.

cards.heading: A reputation in Empire City
cards.text: The karma system reflects moral decisions through Cole's powers, appearance and public reputation. Citizens may fear or celebrate him according to his actions. Choices made during the story therefore affect how the player experiences the city and how the hero is seen within it.

main.title: Wii MotionPlus
main.summary: The Wii MotionPlus is an expansion device for the Wii Remote, the primary game controller for the Wii. The device allows more complex motion to be interpreted than the Wii Remote can do alone. Both the Wii and its successor, the Wii U, support the Wii MotionPlus accessory in games. The accessory was first released in June 2009. A later hardware revision of the Wii Remote, the Wii Remote Plus, was later released with the Wii MotionPlus technology built-in.

cards.heading: Adding MotionPlus to the Remote
cards.text: The Wii MotionPlus is an expansion device for the Wii Remote, the primary game controller for the Wii. The device allows more complex motion to be interpreted than the Wii Remote can do alone. Both the Wii and its successor, the Wii U, support the Wii MotionPlus accessory in games. The accessory was first released in June 2009. A later hardware revision of the Wii Remote, the Wii Remote Plus, was later released with the Wii MotionPlus technology built-in.

cards.heading: Measuring rotational motion
cards.text: The device incorporates a dual-axis tuning fork gyroscope, and a single-axis gyroscope which can determine rotational motion. The information captured by the angular rate sensor can then be used to distinguish true linear motion from the accelerometer readings. This allows for the capture of more complex movements than possible with the Wii Remote alone.

cards.heading: Keeping the extension connector
cards.text: The Wii MotionPlus features a pass-through External Extension Connector, allowing other expansions such as the Nunchuk or Classic Controller to be used simultaneously with the device. When attached to the (original, non-MotionPlus) Wii Remote, the add-on unit extends the length of the controller body by approximately 1.5 in (4 cm). Each Wii MotionPlus includes a longer version of the Wii Remote Jacket to accommodate the added length, and according to Nintendo, the Wii MotionPlus is unsafe to use without it. However, the newer Wii Remote Plus eliminates the need for such elongated jackets by integrating the MotionPlus technology into the Remote itself.

cards.heading: Software designed for the sensor
cards.text: The device is only used by games that have been specifically developed to use its functionality. The title screens of these games also provide an option to access a series of instructional videos created by Nintendo to help players learn how to attach and remove the accessory, recalibrate it, connect external controllers to it or otherwise disconnect them.

main.title: Infinite Space
main.subtitle: A life measured in star systems
main.summary: Infinite Space is Nude Maker and PlatinumGames' Nintendo DS science-fiction role-playing game following Yuri from a young traveller into the command of a growing fleet. His journey crosses the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds and becomes entangled in conflicts far larger than his original ambition. Ships and crew are customisable, while dialogue and decisions shape parts of the route and the people who join. The portable format carries an unusually broad space opera, using the organisation of a fleet to connect personal growth with the scale of interstellar events.

cards.heading: A life measured in star systems
cards.text: Infinite Space is Nude Maker and PlatinumGames' Nintendo DS science-fiction role-playing game following Yuri from a young traveller into the command of a growing fleet. His journey crosses the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds and becomes entangled in conflicts far larger than his original ambition. Ships and crew are customisable, while dialogue and decisions shape parts of the route and the people who join. The portable format carries an unusually broad space opera, using the organisation of a fleet to connect personal growth with the scale of interstellar events.

cards.heading: The fleet answers to its preparation
cards.text: The player travels between planets and issues commands in real-time ship battles rather than directly steering an individual craft. Choosing ships, arranging their capabilities and assigning crew therefore has consequences once an encounter begins. The touchscreen handles the selection of destinations and orders, giving the adventure the feel of directing activity from a command interface. A successful fleet needs more than a collection of impressive hulls. Its preparation has to support the actions available during a fight and the sequence in which those orders can be used.

cards.heading: People keep the ships travelling
cards.text: Crew fatigue increases during travel and reduces efficiency, while stopping at a port restores the fleet and its people. The journey is consequently a sequence of departures and necessary returns to inhabited places. Decisions can also determine which characters join Yuri, making the growing organisation part of the story's response to the player. Static illustrated conversations and three-dimensional travel or battles operate at different scales. Infinite Space uses that contrast to keep the people visible inside a game whose most immediate symbols of progress are large spacecraft and distant destinations.

main.title: Guitar Hero Smash Hits
main.subtitle: The encore becomes a full-band performance
main.summary: Guitar Hero Smash Hits arrived in North America on June 16, 2009 for PlayStation 2, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Wii. Developed by Beenox, it revisited the earlier Guitar Hero games with 48 master recordings, extending songs once played on guitar into performances for guitar, bass, drums and vocals. Queen’s Killer Queen, The Police’s Message in a Bottle and DragonForce’s Through the Fire and Flames connected the compilation to different stages of the series’ history.

cards.heading: Familiar songs, newly shared roles
cards.text: Guitar Hero Smash Hits arrived in North America on June 16, 2009 for PlayStation 2, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Wii. Developed by Beenox, it revisited the earlier Guitar Hero games with 48 master recordings, extending songs once played on guitar into performances for guitar, bass, drums and vocals. Queen’s Killer Queen, The Police’s Message in a Bottle and DragonForce’s Through the Fire and Flames connected the compilation to different stages of the series’ history.

cards.heading: A playable retrospective
cards.text: Additional instrumental roles let players share songs previously played on guitar alone. Band Career provides a cooperative structure, while the original release also offered online battles between two four-player bands and the Music Studio tools from World Tour. Known as Greatest Hits in some regions, the game brought the earlier repertoire into the series' full-band format.
